topology: PC1 and PC2 reach R1 through independent management LANs. R1 Gi0/1 routes server data separately from HTTPS TCP 443; Loopback10 is created, edited, deleted and restored through actual API requests.
implemented: Local privilege-15 operator and privilege-1 observer, RESTCONF, local HTTP authentication, HTTPS enabled and plaintext HTTP disabled.
The browser client now exposes GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE, editable guided JSON examples, media headers and a bounded downloadable credential-free transaction transcript.
GET root and encoded interface key return actual YANG JSON, addresses, operational state and counters. Hostname PATCH/readback/restoration shares IOS and diagram state.
POST creates a real Loopback10 route, returns201 with Location and requires fresh delivered ping replies. Duplicate POST returns409 resource-denied without mutation.
PATCH merges a description while preserving IP; PUT replaces the selected interface, clears omitted description and requires GET plus fresh ICMP verification.
Invalid multi-interface edits reject atomically, preserving data-interface state and real routed connectivity.
PUT enabled=false withdraws actual server forwarding; PATCH enabled=true and fresh delivered replies prove recovery over the separate management path.
DELETE with an empty body now works; removed virtual interfaces return404 on GET and lose their route. Recreate/restore requires fresh IP replies.
Unsupported Accept and Content-Type produce406/415. Wrong credentials and the observer produce401 with the Basic challenge.
HTTP access-class returns403 for PC1 while PC2 HTTPS and PC1 data pings work; an ingress TCP443 ACL instead fails transport without an HTTP status. Both repairs require a fresh successful PC1 GET.

Request outcomes are correlated to actual matching TCP request/reply events, and before/after interface-only snapshots never contain account credentials. Runtime retains at most100 requests and is cleared on portable save/load.
